findings.title: Group view permission grants realm-wide management
findings.body: `canManage()` evaluates the all-groups resource with both `VIEW` and `MANAGE` as acceptable scopes. Consequently, an administrator granted only `VIEW` on all groups is treated as having global manage permission; `canManage(GroupModel)` calls this method first and then allows updates, child creation, and other management operations on every group. Only the `MANAGE` scope should satisfy this check.

findings.title: Group view filtering collects authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` iterates group resources but passes each authorization resource's internal ID to `hasPermission()` and adds that ID to the returned set. `hasPermission()` looks up resources by name, while group resources are named with the actual group ID, and user searches apply this returned set as group IDs. Thus per-group member-view grants do not correctly constrain user searches/counts: the actual group members can be omitted, and the returned authorization IDs are not valid group IDs. Use the resource name (the group ID) for evaluation and collection, and handle the all-groups resource separately.
